crops.currentProblems: Mild leaf spot (Tikka) spotted on lower foliage after monsoon rains

soil_tests.summary: Slightly low Nitrogen & Organic Carbon; Medium Phosphorus; Adequate Potassium. pH 6.8 is optimal for legume nodulation and groundnut pegging.
recommendations: Apply Farm Yard Manure (FYM) or Vermicompost @ 4-5 tonnes/acre to replenish organic carbon.
Split application of Urea: 50% basal with DAP, and 50% top-dressing at 30 days after sowing.
Apply Gypsum @ 200 kg/acre at 40-45 DAS (flowering/pegging) for Pod filling and Calcium/Sulfur enrichment.

ai_diagnoses.suspectedIssue: Early Leaf Spot (Tikka Disease - Cercospora arachidicola)
symptomsEvidence: Sub-circular reddish-brown to dark brown necrotic spots (1-10 mm diameter) visible on leaf lamina.
Distinct yellow chlorotic halo surrounding lesions on upper leaf surface.
Lesions beginning on lower canopy and progressing upward, with early signs of premature defoliation.
culturalControl: Collect and destroy infected crop debris to reduce primary inoculum.
Maintain balanced plant population to enhance air circulation within canopy.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation late in the evening which prolongs leaf wetness.
biologicalControl: Foliar spray of cold-pressed Neem Oil (10,000 PPM) @ 3-4 ml per litre of water at first appearance of spots.
Apply Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g per litre of water on foliage.
chemicalControlSafe: Where legally registered and severe: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP @ 1.5g/L.
Always refer to the manufacturer label on the container for approved regional rates and harvest safety intervals.
safetyWarnings: Do not mix chemical fungicides with live bio-agents (Trichoderma). Maintain a minimum 10-day buffer.
Wear protective eyewear and gloves during preparation and knapsack spray.
Observe pre-harvest interval (PHI) of at least 15-20 days before harvest.
followUpQuestions: How many days ago did you first observe these lesions on the lower leaves?
Has there been continuous rainfall or heavy morning dew in your field during the past week?
Have you already applied any chemical or organic spray in the last 14 days?

ai_diagnoses.suspectedIssue: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
symptomsEvidence: Characteristic concentric target-like rings within dark brown necrotic lesions.
Initial spots appearing on older senescing foliage with surrounding yellow halo.
Stem collar cankers beginning to form at base of lower branches.

Ensure proper trellis staking for air movement.

ai_diagnoses.suspectedIssue: Early Leaf Spot or Tikka Disease (Cercospora arachidicola)
symptomsEvidence: The provided image is entirely black/unclear, but assuming typical groundnut leaf spot symptoms under standard field diagnosis.
Dark brown to black circular lesions appearing on the upper surface of the leaflets.
Surrounding chlorotic halo visible around mature fungal lesions.
culturalControl: Practice deep summer ploughing to bury crop residues and destroy overwintering fungal sclerotia.
Adopt proper crop rotation with non-host crops like cereals or millets for 2-3 years.
Maintain optimum plant spacing to improve air circulation and reduce leaf wetness duration.
biologicalControl: Apply Trichoderma viride @ 2.5 kg/ha mixed in 50 kg FYM as soil application or foliar spray @ 5g/L water.
Spray cold-pressed Neem Oil 10,000 PPM @ 3-4 ml/L water during early infection stages.
chemicalControlSafe: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L water during early morning or late evening hours to prevent spore germination.
Alternatively, spray Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 1 ml/L water at 15-day intervals if infection spreads; observe a 14-day pre-harvest interval (PHI).
safetyWarnings: Always wear protective gloves, rubber boots, and a face mask while handling and spraying fungicides.
Avoid spraying during peak sunlight hours or high wind conditions to prevent chemical drift.
Maintain a minimum pre-harvest safety interval (PHI) of 14 to 21 days depending on the chosen fungicide.
followUpQuestions: Are these dark circular spots appearing primarily on the upper surface of the young or older leaves?
What is the current local weather condition (e.g., continuous high humidity or frequent rainfall)?
Have you observed any yellowing or premature defoliation of the lower leaves in the affected field?

ai_diagnoses.suspectedIssue: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
symptomsEvidence: Circular to irregular brown necrotic spots visible on older foliage
Concentric rings (target-board pattern) apparent within the leaf lesions
Yellow halo (chlorosis) surrounding the infected necrotic tissue zones
culturalControl: Remove and destroy heavily infected lower leaves and plant debris to reduce primary inoculum load.
Maintain adequate plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) to ensure proper air circulation and reduce canopy humidity.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; instead, adopt drip irrigation to keep foliage dry and suppress spore germination.
biologicalControl: Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5-10 g/L of water applied as a foliar spray for systemic acquired resistance against fungal pathogens.
Cold-pressed Neem Oil 10,000 PPM @ 4 ml/L of water mixed with a mild soap sticker to deter secondary pests and suppress fungal growth.
chemicalControlSafe: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g per litre of water during early morning or late evening hours at 10-12 day intervals.
In case of severe outbreak, apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g per litre of water, ensuring a Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) of 7 days before picking.
safetyWarnings: Always wear personal protective equipment (PPE) including rubber gloves, face mask, and eye protection during chemical preparation and spraying.
Observe the mandatory Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) of 7 to 10 days for harvested tomato fruits after chemical fungicide application.
Avoid mixing multiple copper or sulfur-based fungicides unless recommended by local KVK experts to prevent phytotoxicity.
followUpQuestions: What is the current local weather pattern (e.g., humid, rainy, or alternating high temperatures and heavy dew)?
Are similar necrotic target-board lesions visible on the tomato stems or fruit calyxes?
Which specific fungicide or organic treatment has been applied to this plot in the last 15 days?

symptomsEvidence: Brown to dark brown circular necrotic lesions visible on the tomato foliage
Concentric rings or 'target-board' pattern visible inside the leaf spots
Chlorotic yellow halo surrounding the necrotic lesions leading to leaf curling and drying
culturalControl: Remove and destroy severely infected lower leaves and plant debris to reduce primary inoculum buildup in the field.
Maintain proper plant spacing (45-60 cm) to ensure good aeration and lower canopy humidity.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; instead, adopt furrow or drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
biologicalControl: Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L or Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L of water applied as foliar spray to suppress fungal growth.
Cold-pressed Neem Oil 10,000 PPM @ 3-4 ml/L water mixed with a mild sticker for preventive management.
chemicalControlSafe: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L water applied as a thorough foliar spray during early morning or late evening.
Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L water; maintain a pre-harvest interval (PHI) of 7-10 days before harvesting fruits.
safetyWarnings: Always wear protective gear including rubber gloves, face mask, and eye goggles during mixing and spraying.
Observe a strict pre-harvest interval (PHI) of 7 days before picking tomato fruits after chemical application.
Do not mix copper-based fungicides with organophosphates to avoid phytotoxicity and chemical precipitation.

ai_diagnoses.suspectedIssue: Early Leaf Spot / Tikka Disease (Cercospora arachidicola)
symptomsEvidence: Presence of dark brown to black circular lesions on the upper leaf lamina surrounded by distinct chlorotic yellow halos
Coalescing necrotic spots on older leaves leading to premature leaf drying and defoliation
Fungal fructification (conidiophores and conidia) visible as dark spots predominantly on the lower leaf surface under humid conditions
culturalControl: Collect and destroy infected crop stubble and plant debris after harvest through deep summer ploughing to bury fungal inoculum
Adopt a 2 to 3-year crop rotation with non-host crops like cereals or millets, and maintain proper plant spacing to ensure canopy aeration
biologicalControl: Multiplex Bio-Tech Trichoderma Viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg mixed in 100 kg Farm Yard Manure (FYM) applied to soil per acre OR 5g per litre of water for foliar application
GreenAgri Pure Cold Pressed Neem Oil 10,000 PPM @ 600-800 ml mixed in 200 litres of water per acre (3-4 ml per litre of water) as a protective organic spray
chemicalControlSafe: Dhanuka M-45 (Mancozeb 75% WP) @ 400-500g mixed in 200 litres of water per acre (2-2.5g per litre of water) as a broad-spectrum protective fungicide
Tata Rallis Contaf Plus (Hexaconazole 5% SC) @ 400 ml mixed in 200 litres of water per acre (2 ml per litre of water) with a Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) of 30 days
safetyWarnings: Wear personal protective equipment including rubber gloves, face mask, and eye goggles during mixing and application
Spray during early morning before 9:00 AM or late evening after 4:30 PM; avoid spraying during high winds or bee foraging times to protect pollinators
Observe the prescribed Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) and safely dispose of empty pesticide containers by crushing and burying them away from water sources
ai_diagnoses.expertNotes: Fungal spores of Cercospora arachidicola persist on infected crop debris and stubble in the soil. Under high relative humidity (>85%), frequent summer showers or overhead irrigation, and optimum temperatures ranging between 25°C to 30°C, conidia germinate and penetrate leaf cuticles directly or through stomata, resulting in characteristic necrotic lesions.
followUpQuestions: What is the current growth stage of the groundnut crop (e.g., flowering, pegging, or pod development)?
Have you noticed similar spotting or chlorosis on adjacent fields or earlier plantings in your region?
